extracted.intended_audience: Prospective and current Kirschstein-NRSA individual fellowship applicants, sponsoring institutions (AORs), sponsors/mentors, and NIH/IC administrative staff
extracted.subtask_description: Policies, application requirements, review criteria, award administration, allowable costs, and trainee obligations for NIH Kirschstein-NRSA individual fellowships (F-series, F99/K00, etc.). Covers application submission, RCR requirements, review scoring, payments, allowances, and limits on support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active military duty applicants policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH does not restrict career military personnel from applying for Kirschstein-NRSA individual fellowship awards while on active military duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At time of application, the applicant’s branch must submit a letter endorsing the application and indicating willingness to continue normal active duty pay and allowances during requested fellowship. If awarded, NIH will pay institutional allowance and necessary tuition/fees; stipends, health insurance, and travel allowances are not allowable charges to the fellowship for career military personnel. Payment of concurrent benefits by NIH to active-duty career military recipients is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission format and emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fellowship applicant must submit an application based on the NOFO application package using Grants.gov with SF424 (R&R) components plus the PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major emphasis should be the research training experience and broadening of scientific competence. The AOR agrees to secure and retain (but need not submit to NIH) assurance signatures of applicant and sponsor. Postdoctoral applicants' assurance includes certification of having read payback information and agreeing to payback provisions if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with public policy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship applicants and sponsoring institutions must comply with policies governing civil rights, human subjects protection, research misconduct, humane care and use of vertebrate animals, inclusion policies, human embryonic stem cells, recombinant or synthetic nucleic molecules, and other applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete list of applicable requirements is in Exhibit 4, Public Policy Requirements, Objectives and Appropriation Mandates in IIA; applicants must follow those policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons registration and PI Role
rubrics_metrics.description: All fellowship applicants and sponsoring institutions must be registered in the eRA Commons; the fellowship applicant must be assigned the 'PI Role' in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the PI Role provides appropriate access to the application and review information. If applicant is submitting through a different sponsoring institution, they must be affiliated with that sponsoring institution in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID iD requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: ORCID identifiers are required at time of application for individual fellowships (including F05, F30, F31, F32, F33, F37, F38, F99/K00, FI2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eRA validations will check for ORCID iDs and applications will not be accepted unless an ORCID iD is linked to the PD/PI's eRA Commons Personal Profile. Applicants may link or create ORCID accounts via eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At least three (but no more than five) letters of reference must be submitted on behalf of the fellowship applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference letters are submitted directly by referees through the eRA Commons (separate electronic process) and are joined with the application in eRA once submission completes. Missing required letters may delay review or result in non-acceptance. Applicants must follow the Individual Fellowship Application Guide instructions sent to prospective referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: All fellowship applicants must include a plan to obtain instruction in the responsible conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must document prior instruction (with dates) and propose future instruction. It must address five components: format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency. It may include career-stage-appropriate individualized instruction or independent scholarly activities. The sponsor/mentor's role in RCR instruction must be described. Applications without an RCR plan are incomplete and may be delayed; unacceptable plans will not be funded until revised and acceptable. Consult the NOFO for additional instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR format expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion-based instruction with substantive face-to-face interaction is expected for RCR training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video conferencing may be incorporated if it fosters discussion, active learning, engagement and interaction, but video conferencing should not be the sole means to meet the requirement except in short-term training programs or unusual, well-justified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter topics
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR instruction should include a broad set of topics reflecting developments in research conduct and research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested topics include: conflict of interest and commitment; policies regarding human subjects, vertebrate animals, and lab safety; mentor/mentee responsibilities; safe research environments (free of harassment); collaborative research (including industry and international collaborations); peer review responsibilities and confidentiality; data acquisition and analysis and laboratory tools and recordkeeping practices; secure and ethical data use, data management, sharing, and ownership; research misconduct and policies; responsible authorship and publication; the scientist's role in society and environmental/societal impacts of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR faculty participation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and appropriate faculty are highly encouraged to contribute to formal and informal RCR instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal instruction occurs through laboratory interactions year-round. Sponsors may act as discussion leaders, speakers, lecturers, or course directors in formal instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR duration expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should involve substantive contact hours between the fellow, sponsor and faculty; acceptable programs generally involve at least eight contact hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A semester-long series of seminars/programs may be more effective than a single seminar or one-day workshop to allow sufficient depth, consolidation, and synthesis of topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR frequency expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR instruction should be undertaken at least once during each career stage and at a frequency of no less than once every four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are encouraged to provide ongoing and discipline-specific training as researchers progress; advanced trainees may receive more tailored, discipline-specific RCR training relevant to their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent applications restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may not have two or more competing NRSA individual fellowship applications pending review concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSR will not accept for review any application that is essentially the same as one already reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt dates and review timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirschstein-NRSA individual fellowship applications undergo a review process that takes 5 to 8 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual schedule for receipt, review, and award is in the specific NOFO and on NIH's Standard Due Dates website; applicants should consult those for deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific peer review by SRG
rubrics_metrics.description: Each new and renewal individual fellowship application will be evaluated for scientific merit by an NIH Scientific Review Group (SRG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRG assigns scores and provides summary statements used in funding considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact scoring standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score reflecting likelihood that the fellowship will enhance the applicant’s potential for a productive independent scientific research career in a health-related field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall impact is considered in light of the scored and additional review criteria. Major considerations include the candidate’s potential for a productive career, the candidate’s need for proposed training, and the degree to which the research training proposed, the sponsor, and the environment will satisfy those needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criteria for fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers give separate scores for each of three scored review criteria: Candidate's Preparedness and Potential; Research Training Plan; Commitment to Candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These scored criteria apply primarily to F30, F31, F32, F33 and F99/K00 applications. Consult the NOFO for additional detail about each criterion and for criteria for other fellowship types (e.g., F05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional (non-scored) review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider the following items in determining scientific and technical merit but will not give separate scores: Protections for Human Subjects; Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Individuals Across the Lifespan; Vertebrate Animals; Biohazards; Resubmission Applications; Renewal Applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NOFO for additional information describing each relevant additional review criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (not for overall impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will address but not score these items and should not consider them when providing the overall impact score: Training in RCR; Select Agents Research; Resource Sharing Plans; Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources; Budget and Period Support; Foreign Sponsoring Institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NOFO for information describing relevant additional review considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary level of review for funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: IC staff provide secondary review for award decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria used include the SRG’s recommendation/overall merit, relevance to the IC’s research training priorities and program balance, and availability of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and inquiries process
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows receive email notification when SRG recommendation/impact score and summary statement are available in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about initial review recommendations and funding possibilities should be directed to the designated IC Program Official (PO), not to the SRO of the SRG. If under consideration for funding, NIH will request any additional necessary information; after issues resolved NoA will be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on aggregate period of support
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual may receive more than 5 years of aggregate NRSA support at the predoctoral level and 3 years at the postdoctoral level (including combination of institutional and individual NRSA support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For individual MD/PhD or other dual-doctoral degree fellowships (F30), individuals may receive up to 6 years aggregate NRSA support at the predoctoral level. Over dual-degree duration, at least 50% of award period must be devoted to graduate research training. Matriculation timing requirements apply for eligibility; exceptions require IC waiver with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to maximum support
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions to maximum period of support require a waiver from the NIH awarding IC based on justification from the individual and sponsoring institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be made in writing by the AOR, specify additional support amount sought, and include signatures of fellow and sponsor. Generally recognized exceptions include: (1) Physicians/Clinicians who need additional time to complete training (contingent on good academic standing and justification); (2) Interruptions/Breaks in service due to unavoidable events (loss of preceptor, illness, accident) that significantly detracted from training and a short extension would permit completion. Other exceptions require exceptionally strong justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All fellows are required to pursue their research training full time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-time is generally defined as devoting at least 40 hours per week to research training activities or as specified by the sponsoring institution's policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time training policy and approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Part-time NRSA training may be permitted in certain circumstances with NIH awarding IC approval in advance of each budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be written, signed by fellow, AOR and sponsor, justify need (e.g., medical, disability, personal/family situations such as child/elder care), provide expected duration and assurances of intent to return to full-time and complete the training. Part-time training will not be approved to accommodate other funding, jobs, clinical practice or responsibilities at sponsoring institution. NRSA support is not permissible for less than 50% effort; individuals reducing below 50% must take a leave of absence. NIH will issue revised NoA with prorated stipend for approved part-time periods and part-time may affect service obligation accrual/repayment for postdocs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation of award and required forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship activation may occur on or after the Federal award date up to the latest activation date in the NoA (generally 6 months); Activation Notice and (for postdocs in first 12 months) Payback Agreement must be submitted when training begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stipend may not be paid until forms are submitted and the fellow begins training. Activation Notice and Payback Agreement may be submitted up to 30 days before start for payroll purposes; any change in start date must be immediately reported. If award conditioned on degree completion, proof of degree must be submitted with Activation Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment responsibilities by institution type
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment method depends on sponsoring institution type: non-Federal non-profit institutions receive award and disburse stipend and other costs; Federal laboratories’ fellows are paid stipends directly by the NIH awarding IC through PMS; foreign fellows are paid stipends directly by awarding IC through PMS while institutional allowance is awarded to sponsoring institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government-owned but contract-operated facilities are not considered Federal laboratories; sponsoring institution in those cases would be the contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award cost restrictions for fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-award costs to an individual fellowship are limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipends and tuition/fees may not be charged to a fellowship award until the fellow has activated the award and appropriate paperwork submitted; these costs may never be charged as pre-award. Rare occasions may allow institutional allowance pre-award costs—sponsoring institutions should consult the NIH awarding IC when considering pre-award costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend purpose and payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A stipend is a subsistence allowance to help defray living expenses during research training and is not provided as a condition of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipends must be paid according to NIH stipend levels based on 12-month full-time appointment; in event of early termination stipend prorated. Institutions may hire NRSA trainees as employees and provide benefits consistent with other employees, but stipend policy does not intend to discourage this. Sponsoring institution must base stipend calculations on NIH stipend level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend level determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend levels are updated periodically; predoctoral uses a single level for all predoctoral candidates; postdoctoral stipend level is determined by number of full years of relevant postdoctoral experience at award issuance; senior fellows' stipend must be commensurate with their base salary but not exceed NRSA limit for 7+ years experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once stipend level is set it must be paid for the entire grant year and does not change mid-year; NIH awarding IC will adjust awards on anniversary dates to applicable stipend amounts. Relevant experience may include research, teaching assistantship, internships, residency, clinical duties, or other health-related work beyond qualifying degree. NIH support does not provide fringe benefits for senior fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional allowance purpose and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH awards an institutional allowance to help support training costs; it is a fixed amount and expenditures under it are not subject to NIH prior approval and need not be accounted for on an actual-cost basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for Federal training sites, sponsoring institution administers allowance and may expend up to full allowance upon activation. If fellow not in training for >6 months of award year, only half the institutional allowance may be charged. For Federal training sites, NIH awarding IC authorizes and administers allowance through PMS. Allowable uses vary by institution type (non-Federal public/private nonprofit; Federal labs; for-profit institutions) and include items such as research supplies, equipment, travel to scientific meetings, health insurance; see institution-type guidance for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of institutional allowance—travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel to scientific meetings is an appropriate use of institutional allowance when necessary for the individual’s training and costs are incurred within the period of grant-supported training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fellows at Federal laboratories, travel reimbursement must follow applicable Federal travel regulations. Funds may not be used for commuting between residence and training institution except that sponsoring institution may authorize one-way travel allowance in extreme hardship cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of institutional allowance—health insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellow’s health insurance is an allowable institutional allowance cost if applied consistently to all individuals in similar training status regardless of funding source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family health insurance is allowable for fellows with families and eligible for family coverage; self-only insurance allowed for fellows without families. Health insurance can include vision or dental if consistent with organizational policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of institutional allowance—medical liability and special insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical liability (malpractice) or other special insurance is allowable only if nature of the research training requires such insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: medical liability allowable if training involves direct contact with patients or human subjects. For cost to be charged to NRSA, it must be consistently required for all in similar training status. Optional employee-benefit insurances (disability, life insurance, worker's comp) are not normally allowable unless nature of research training requires them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of institutional allowance—extraordinary costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions may request additional funds when training involves extraordinary costs for travel to remote field sites or accommodations for fellows with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested funds must be reasonable relative to total award and directly related to the approved research training project; additional funds provided only in exceptional, fully justified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition and fees policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition and fees are provided at specified percentages and caps depending on fellowship level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predoctoral (F30/F31): 60% of actual tuition up to $16,000/year (or up to $21,000/year for formally combined dual-degree programs). Postdoctoral (F32) and senior fellowships (F33): 60% up to $4,500/year, or up to $16,000/year if enrolled in a postdoctoral formal degree program. For postdoctoral fellows, tuition/fees allowable only if required for specific courses supporting research training. Health insurance is not part of tuition/fees (charged under institutional allowance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel to foreign training sites
rubrics_metrics.description: For fellows at foreign training sites, awards may include a single economy/coach round-trip fare; no allowance for dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. flag air carriers must be used to the maximum extent possible when commercial air is used between U.S. and foreign countries. Travel funds must be reported on the Termination Notice as part of the stipend amount. See Cost Considerations for more foreign travel guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Childcare costs allowable conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Childcare costs are allowable for full-time NRSA fellows and full-time recipients of F99/K00 during the F99 phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/recipients may request childcare costs in new, continuation, or administrative supplement applications. Childcare must be provided by a licensed childcare provider; recipients must maintain documentation (e.g., proof of license) available to NIH upon request (but not submitted each request). Childcare costs are not tied to payback obligations and should not be reported as such. When awarded, childcare funds are generally restricted and cannot be re-budgeted without prior written NIH awarding IC approval; unused childcare funds at early termination remain unobligated and will be adjusted in closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee benefits unallowable on fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs normally associated with employee benefits (FICA, worker's compensation, life insurance, union dues, unemployment insurance) may not be charged to individual fellowship awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a fellow requests institution deduct such costs from stipend (e.g., union dues), institution may provide the service but deductions cannot be made automatically without fellow approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting restrictions for individual fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual fellowship awards are formula-based, generally budget-category restricted, and cannot be rebudgeted without prior written approval from the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipends must be expended using the NIH-provided stipend level; no funds can be rebudgeted into stipend to change stipend level. When fellowship terminates early, unexpended stipends must be returned and cannot be rebudgeted. Institutional allowance is fixed; unexpended allowance may only be rebudgeted into tuition and fees when tuition/fees have been awarded.
